final.after_tax_hurdle: 21% federal tax cost on realized gains versus the need to manage concentration risk [D04, D08]

drivers.driver: The position has grown to a dominant weight in the equity portfolio, requiring prudent trimming to manage concentration [D08].
Tax planning in a high-valuation market warrants realizing gains on a portion of the holding [D04].
The business remains a wonderful franchise, but the stock is fully priced, making it a logical source of liquidity [D04, D05].

final.memo:
Apple remains a wonderful business with an ecosystem that continues to generate impressive returns on capital and growing service revenues [D01, D03]. We do not sell businesses that we admire because Mr. Market is enthusiastic, but we must remain disciplined regarding the concentration of our portfolio and the tax consequences of our holdings [D04, D08]. 

With the position representing roughly half of our listed equity portfolio, prudence dictates that we trim our exposure [D08]. While a 21% federal tax hit is significant, it is a known cost that we accept to improve our portfolio balance in a fully-priced market [D04]. This decision is not a reflection of a change in the underlying business economics, which remain highly regarded, but a reflection of size and capital allocation realities [D01, D05, D08]. 

We continue to hold a substantial residual position in what we consider an outstanding consumer franchise [D01, D08]. Our goal is to ensure that Berkshire maintains the liquidity and diversification necessary to navigate whatever the future may bring, without risking permanent loss of capital or reputation [D04].
